newsitem.title: USA: July US jobs figures no sign of overheating - Herman.
newsitem.headline: July US jobs figures no sign of overheating - Herman.

text.p: U.S. Labor Secretary Alexis Herman said on Friday a strong set of July labor market data gave no hint of the economy overheating and that wage growth over the past year did not signal any inflationary pressures.

"For the past 12 months you have seen a growth of only 3.6 percent (in average hourly earnings). I don't believe it indicates any signs of real inflationary pressures on the economy," she told Reuters Financial Television.
"I don't see any overheating in today's data," Herman added. "Real wages were actually flat for this month. It's the same steady performance we've seen for the past 12 months."

The government earlier reported that the U.S. unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent in July from 5.0 percent in the previous month, while non-farm payrolls rose by an unexpectedly strong 316,000 in July. ((-- Washington newsroom 202 898-8377))
